title: Related-Key Adaptation of a 10-Round AES-256 Attack
summary: An existing 10-round AES-256 attack is formulated in the related-subkey model; adapting it to the more standard related-key model remains open.

formal_statement.body: For $10$-round AES-256, an existing attack is formulated in the related-subkey model rather than the more standard related-key model. Determine whether this attack can be modified to operate in the related-key model.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of 10-round AES-256 in related-subkey and related-key attack models.
parameters: 10 rounds — round count of the targeted AES-256 variant
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the existing attack can be modified from the related-subkey model to the related-key model.

citations.label: Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds

progress.summary: The paper lists this question in its Conclusions and Open Problems section, asking whether its 10-round AES-256 attack can be moved from the related-subkey model to the more standard related-key model.
citation_labels: Alex Biryukov et al., Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds
